rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After prior peoples’ destruction established the messengers’ truth and God’s power, the challenge denies that creating and ending life could weary Him or prevent resurrection.
rows.anchor: فثبت صدق الرسل وثبتت القدرة على كل ما يريد سبحانه بهذا الخلق من الإيجاد والإعدام أنكر عليهم التكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first creation includes the heavens, earth, humanity, animals, and their successive stages; people wrongly infer from customary difficulty that resurrection is impossible.
rows.anchor: من السماوات والأرض وما بينهما حين ابتدأناه اختراعا من العدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb عيي means failing to find one’s way or intended result, being unable, or lacking capacity to master something.
rows.anchor: عيي بالأمر - إذا لم يهتد لأمره أو لوجه مراده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical answer implies perfected creation already proves capacity and resurrection, while deniers remain trapped in severe confusion and incoherent speech.
rows.anchor: أي خلط شديد وشبهة موجبة للتكلم بكلام مختلط لا يعقل له معنى

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali tells his neighbor that truth is the way to recognize its people, when warning that the neighbor is confused.
rows.anchor: قال علي رضي الله عنه : يا جار , إنه لملبوس عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan persuades them that resurrection is outside ordinary experience, so they abandon the sound analogy that what is harder to originate can be repeated.
rows.anchor: ولبس الشيطان عليهم تسويله لهم أن البعث خارج عن العادة فتركوا لذلك القياس الصحيح والحكم بطريقة الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity is an especially wondrous, comprehensive creation, combining intimacy and arrogance, memory and forgetfulness, ignorance and knowledge, obedience and disobedience; God appoints guardians over every state.
rows.anchor: وهو أعجب خلقا وأجمع من جميع ما مضى ذكره بما فيه من الأنس والطغيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows hidden thoughts now and in the future, even before they emerge from the unseen into the soul’s secret store; a person may not control them himself.
rows.anchor: الآن وفيما بعد ذلك مما لم ينقدح بعد من خزائن الغيب إلى سر النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers’ hearts know God’s power, the Qur’an’s truth and inimitability, and the Messenger’s veracity; envy, rivalry, pride, and ambition drive their habitual verbal denial.
rows.anchor: أن قلوبهم عالمة بقدرتنا على أكمل ما نريد وبصحة القرآن وإعجازه وصدق الرسول به صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s nearness here is nearness of knowledge and witness, without spatial distance; unlike bodily parts, nothing can screen anything from His knowledge.
rows.anchor: قرب علم وشهود من غير مسافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression is generic: the two jugular veins lie like ropes along the front sides of the neck, extending from the head to the heart’s great vein.
rows.anchor: والوريدان عرقان كالحبلين مكتنفان لصفحتي العنق في مقدمها متصلات من الرأس إلى الوتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jugular is an image of extreme closeness, and the annexation follows the pattern of the expression مسجد الجامع.
rows.anchor: وهذا مثل في فرط القرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author points back to his useful discussion of the same divine protection in al-Māʾida.
rows.anchor: وقد مضى في تفسري سورة المائدة

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri says the verse brings awe, alarm, and fear to some, but spiritual life, intimacy, and settled hearts to others.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري : وفي هذه الآية هيبة وفزع وخوف لقوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companion answers the expected accusation that he caused the person’s rebellion: he lacked power over him, who was already deeply astray by disposition.
rows.anchor: فإنه لا سلطان لي عليه وأنت أعلم بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person’s innate, pervasive misguidance made him rush toward what angers God without needing even the slightest prompting.
rows.anchor: محيط به من جميع جوانبه لا يمكن رجوعه معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the fully disclosed judgment, God ends their strenuous dispute; new faith can no longer benefit them once the unseen has been unveiled.
rows.anchor: أي لا توقعوا الخصومة بهذا الجد والاجتهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before judgment God had delivered every needed warning, kindly removing ambiguity and leaving no one an excuse.
rows.anchor: أي كل ما ينبغي تقديمه حتى لم يبق لبس ولا تركت لأحد حجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s prior declaration is not changed; forgiving some sinners does not alter a threat, since indications of pardon show that the threat is conditional.
rows.anchor: والعفو عن بعض المذنبين ليس تبديلا لأن دلائل العفو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intensified negation declares God wholly free of injustice toward the companion, the misled person, or anyone else: He neither punishes the undeserving nor breaks His word.
rows.anchor: لا القرين ولا من أطغاه ولا غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question dramatizes Hell’s vast capacity: despite its constriction and hatred of its occupants, it receives uncountable multitudes and seems to welcome their rush into it.
rows.anchor: أن النار كبيرة مع ضيقها , فهي تسع من الخلائق ما لا يقع تحت حصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura’s purpose is to establish the punishment promised under oath in al-Dhāriyāt, whose truth was signaled in Qāf; its occurrence is firmer than the changeable natural signs mentioned here.
rows.anchor: مقصودها تحقيق وقوع العذاب الذي هو مضمون الوعيد المقسم على وقوعه في الذاريات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The title al-Ṭūr best signals this certainty when the oath and its answer are considered, down to their individual wording.
rows.anchor: وقد بان أن اسمها أدل ما يكون على ذلك بملاحظة القسم وجوابه حتى بمفردات الألفاظ في خطابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala calls God the supreme possessor of dominion, universally merciful to those who realize Him, and specially merciful through guidance to the devoted.
rows.anchor: بسم الله } الملك الأعظم ذي الملك والملكوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wail is an expression Arabs use for someone who has fallen into ruin: a shameful affliction that brings lament and grief.
rows.anchor: فويل } هي كلمة يقولونها لمن وقع في الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doomed are those deeply committed to denial who die after calling truthful messengers liars; the intended denial concerns what deserves belief.
rows.anchor: أي العريقين في التكذيب وهم من مات على نسبة الصادقين إلى الكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their words and deeds resemble a person wading in water without knowing where to place a foot; they play at it deliberately, not from bewilderment or grief.
rows.anchor: أي أعمالهم وأقوالهم أعمال الخائض في ماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Confusion and frivolous play together produce falsehood: their speech and actions lack proper place, foundation, and proof.
rows.anchor: فاجتمع عليهم أمران موجبان للباطل : الخوض واللعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are driven harshly and forcefully toward Hell by whatever agents God appoints; repeating the root as دعًّا intensifies and confirms the image.
rows.anchor: أي يدفعون دفعا عنيفا بجفوة وغلظة

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi describes Hell’s keepers raising the sinners’ hands to their necks, gathering their forelocks to their feet, then thrusting them face-first and shoving them from behind.
rows.anchor: قال البغوي : وذلك أن خزنة جهنم يعلون أيديهم إلى أعناقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is portrayed as a grimacing, loathing, coarse, roaring layer that receives them.
rows.anchor: وهي الطبقة التي تلقاهم بالعبوسة والكراهة والغليظ والزفير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire is a burning body that destroys what it touches and occupies its victims’ attention, unlike their former play.
rows.anchor: الجسم المحرق المفسد لما أتى عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their denial of the fire was extreme, the root of their other denials, and repeated continually in worldly life; fronting بها highlights that particular denial.
rows.anchor: ولما كان تكذيبهم بها في أقصى درجات التكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because they obstinately called the Qur’an’s threat magic, they are now taunted: is this burning punishment magic, or are they still blindhearted as before?
rows.anchor: إن القرآن بما فيه من الوعيد سحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Najm opens by directing people to follow the Prophet’s guidance, after al-Ṭūr ended with a command to glorify and praise God and deniers had called the Prophet a soothsayer, sorcerer, or madman.
rows.anchor: افتتحت هذه بالحث على الاهتدا بهدية والاستدلال بدله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-najm may mean the class of celestial stars, the Qur’an revealed in portions (called tanjīm), or vegetation.
rows.anchor: أي هذا الجنس من نجوم السماء أو القرآن

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: If the oath means celestial stars, al-Baghawi cites Ikrima’s report from Ibn Abbas that stars are used against devils when they eavesdrop.
rows.anchor: قال البغوي : الشياطين عند الاستراق كما رواه عكرمة عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa, hawā means to fall; with ḍamma, it means to rise, which suits stars’ setting or ascent and the guidance they provide to worshippers, readers, and travelers.
rows.anchor: هوى هويا - بالتفح إذا سقط , وبالضم - إذا علا وصعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath may also evoke vegetation falling flat or rising from the earth; its wondrous design demonstrates universal power, knowledge, oneness, and absolute independence.
rows.anchor: إن كان المراد النبات , لما فيه من غيريب الصنعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath’s past-tense answer denies the accusations made against the Prophet even before his mission, making the inference from his earlier life especially clear.
rows.anchor: أجابه بقوله معبرا بالماضي نفيا لما كانوا رموه به وليسهل ما قبل النبوة فيكون ما بعدها بطريقة الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author explains the separate verse وجدك ضالا as not knowing, rather than moral misguidance.
rows.anchor: فالمراد غير عالم , وعبر بالصحبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Muhammad “your companion” invites his audience to recall their familiarity with him and makes their accusation implausible given his character and purity.
rows.anchor: وعبر بالصحبة مع كونها أدل على القصد مرغبة لهم فيها ومقبلة بهم إليه ومقبحة عليهم اتهامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He did not deviate even slightly or intend harm; he is guarded from causes of misguidance, including devils.
rows.anchor: وما مال أدنى ميل ولا كان مقصوده مما يسوء فإنه محروس من أسبابه التي هي غواية الشياطين وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says God defended Muhammad, while other prophets had to deny accusations that they were misguided or foolish.
rows.anchor: وأما بقية الأانبياء فدفعوا أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s speech never arises from whim, unlike soothsayers whose lies outweigh their truths, poets, and others; the Qur’an is not self-composed.
rows.anchor: أي يجاوز نطقه فمه في وقت من الأوقات لا في الحال ولا في الاستقبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an, its explanation, and the Prophet’s words, deeds, and states are revelation from God, renewed to him from time to time.
rows.anchor: أي من الله تعالى , وأكده بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet may exercise ijtihād; once his judgment settles, revelation confirms it, so returning his judgment to revelation clears him of acting from whim.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يجتهد صلى الله عليه وسلم , فإذا استقر اجتهاده

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says the oath answers exhausted accusations, then the sura unfolds the Prophet’s closeness to God and rebukes deniers through its later signs and questions.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو جعفر ابن الزبير في برهانه : لما قطع سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who taught the Prophet the revelation was Gabriel, whose extraordinary power makes the Prophet’s instruction remarkable despite his being unlettered.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الوحي ظاهرا فيما بواسطة الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel can carry out everything God commands, displaying a capacity greater than the Prophetic audience had seen.
rows.anchor: فإن معلمه بهذه الصفة التي هو بها بحيث ينفذ كل ما أمره الله به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhū mirra describes firm resolve and tremendous strength to perform and bear the assigned task: concentrated, steady, formidable powers without distraction.
rows.anchor: أي جزم في قوة وقدرة عظيمة على الذهاب فيما أمر به والطاقة لحمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel became upright and balanced in the fullest strength and in the finest condition of the form in which he was created.
rows.anchor: فاستقام واعتدل بغاية ما يكون من قوته على أكمل حالاته في الصورة التي فطر عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The main reading identifies the pronoun with Gabriel at the highest region of heaven; another possible reading identifies the Prophet, with Gabriel standing with him.
rows.anchor: أي والحال أن جبرائيل عليه السلام , وجوزوا أن يكون الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scene is when the Prophet saw Gabriel seated on a chair between heaven and earth, filling the horizon.
rows.anchor: وذلك حين رآه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم جالسا على كرسي بين السماء والأرض قد سد الأفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Then marks the immense, otherwise indescribable approach to the divine presence prepared for receiving revelation, emphasizing its exalted rank.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الدنو من الحضرة الإليهة - التي هي مهيئة لتلقي الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the author’s first reading, Gabriel approached God in increased honor, not spatial distance; divine nearness is not measured by space.
rows.anchor: أي جبرائيل عليه السلام من الجناب الأقدس دنو زيادة في كرامة لا دنو مسافة

rows.speaker: ابن برجان
rows.claim: Ibn Barjan distinguishes divine nearness to each being from a special nearness in which a person hears and sees only what God approves.
rows.anchor: لا يسمع ولا يبصر إلا ما يرضاه - اشار إليه ابن برجان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After receiving the revelation permitted for that time, Gabriel descended as messenger to Muhammad like something lowered by a rope, while retaining his firm connection to the high horizon.
rows.anchor: فأخذ الوحي الذي أذن له في أخذه في ذلك الوقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase measures the apparent closeness from the viewpoint of an observer who sees Gabriel near the Prophet.
rows.anchor: في القرب من صاحبكم في رأي من يراه منكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says qaws means a cubit in the dialect of Azd Shanūʾa.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : القوس الذراع بلغة أزدشنوءة

rows.speaker: ابن برجان
rows.claim: Ibn Barjan defines qāb al-qawsayn as the space between the bow’s two limbs; another explanation measures from the grip to the string.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن برجان : قاب القوسين : ما بين السيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording means a viewer would hesitate and describe Gabriel as even nearer because of the striking closeness.
rows.anchor: بمعنى أن الناظر منكم لو رآه لتردد وقال ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Muslim’s report from Ibn Masʿud says the Prophet saw Gabriel with six hundred wings.
rows.anchor: روى مسلم في الإيمان من صحيحه عن الشيباني قال : ( سألت زر بن حبيش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God secretly conveyed revelation to His servant, meaning Muhammad; the unexpressed antecedent is clear from al-Shūrā’s account of revelation through a messenger, and suits the hidden mode of speech.
rows.anchor: أي ألقى سرا من كلام الله بسبب هذا القرب , وعقبه بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad alone merits this designation here: he never worshipped anyone but God and worshipped Him at Ḥirāʾ and elsewhere.
rows.anchor: لأنه لم يتعبد قط لأحد غير الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author tentatively connects this descent with the first revelation at Ḥirāʾ, when Muhammad was frightened, returned trembling, and asked to be covered.
rows.anchor: هذه النزلة - والله أعلم - كانت على هذا التقدير في أول الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As an alternative to taking the approach and following verbs as Gabriel’s, the pronouns may refer throughout to God, making “His servant” unambiguous.
rows.anchor: ويمكن لأجل احتمال الضمائر لما يناسبها من الظواهر أن يكون ضمير

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari’s Isra report from Anas recounts the Prophet’s chest being opened and filled with faith and wisdom, his ascent through the heavens, and the revelation of fifty prayers, later reduced to five worth ten each.
rows.anchor: روى البخاري في التوحيد في باب { وكلم الله موسى تكليما } عن أنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author favors reading this report’s approacher as God when joined to a later account from Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq: after creation reaches its limit, God’s approach is beyond comprehension and fitting to His majesty.
rows.anchor: وهو في غاية الحسن إذا جمعته مع ما يأتي في هذا الوجه المنقول عن جعفر الصادق رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The language of divine approach and descent represents the easy, gentle transmission reaching Muhammad while he remains connected to the holy realm; it does not assign God a bodily location or likeness.
rows.anchor: فكان الدنو والتدلي تمثيلا لما وصل منه سبحانه إلى عبده محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بغاية السهولة واليسر واللطافة

rows.speaker: عثمان بن أبي العاص
rows.claim: A report in the author’s Juzʾ al-ʿAyshī likens the nightly divine descent and answering of prayers to a king opening doors first to his intimates, then progressively to everyone; the author calls the comparison representational.
rows.anchor: كما رويناه في جزء العيشي من حديث عثمان بن أبي العاص رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is independent of such degrees, has no likeness, and nothing resembles Him; the royal analogy only explains the address in familiar terms.
rows.anchor: وأما من هو غني عن كل شيء فله سبحانه المثل الأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author points to the discussion of Qur’an al-Fajr in al-Isrāʾ for further explanation of this analogy.
rows.anchor: وفي { قرآن الفجر } من سورة سبحان
